headlines.title: 4 arrested in shooting of 49ers player Keion White at San Francisco nightclub
headlines.description: Four suspects have been arrested in connection with the February shooting of San Francisco 49ers player Keion White at a Mission District nightclub, San Francisco officials announced Wednesday. The arrests were made in various cities across California and Georgia following a monthslong investigation that included more than 50 search warrants and assistance from over 250 law enforcement personnel, officials said. White, a defensive lineman for the 49ers, was shot in the early morning hours of Feb. 9 at the Dahlia nightclub, where he was hosting an event after the Super Bowl. “It started when multiple suspects, some brandishing firearms, confronted the 49ers player, which then led to a physical altercation between the group and the victim, who was shot in the leg,” San Francisco police Chief Derrick Lew said. White has since recovered following surgery and has been playing for the 49ers this season. Keion White May 2 Ricky Pearsall Sep 19, 2025 Following several months of investigation, officers last week served four no-bail arrest warrants. Atlanta police arrested 38-year-old Marquis Davis at his home last Wednesday. Officers found an illegal firearm, 820 grams of MDMA, 1,026 grams of methamphetamine, 979 grams of cocaine and 3,842 grams of fentanyl, police said. That same morning, San Francisco police and San Joaquin County sheriff’s deputies arrested 36-year-old Antoine Washington in Stockton. Officers recovered a loaded firearm, more than 120 oxycodone pills and roughly $7,000, according to police. In Southern California on the same day, San Francisco police and Irvine police took 35-year-old Curtis Green into custody without incident. The fourth suspect and alleged shooter, 36-year-old Gregory Walker of Mountain House, was arrested last Friday in Los Angeles, police said. “We will not tolerate any type of violence in our city, but certainly not gun violence,” San Francisco District Attorney Brooke Jenkins said. “We had a great, amazing Super Bowl weekend that ended with this incident. I am just so thankful to the San Francisco police that we are being able to hold those accountable who sadly chose violence on that night.” Walker has since been charged with assault with a firearm with allegations that he personally discharged that firearm at White, Jenkins said. Walker also was charged with possession of a firearm by a felon, possession of a concealed firearm by a felon and possession of a loaded firearm by a felon. Jenkins said the district attorney’s office filed a motion to keep Walker in custody because they believe he poses a public safety risk. A judge agreed during Walker’s first court appearance Wednesday, ordering him to be held without bail for the time being and pushing his formal arraignment to Monday. Walker’s attorney, Jeff Wozniak, said even though Walker was arrested in Los Angeles, he lives in San Francisco and did not do what he’s accused of. “Mr. Walker is a family man, a longshoreman, a union member,” Wozniak said. “We’re going to show that he’s innocent and get him back to his family.” Green faces multiple misdemeanors, including brandishing a firearm and carrying a concealed weapon, Jenkins said. In court, he was ordered to be released from custody. San Francisco police are working with the district attorney’s office and prosecutors in other jurisdictions to arrange for Davis and Washington to be transferred to the city to face charges, Lew said. The February shooting marked the second time in two years that a 49ers player was shot in the city. Wide receiver Ricky Pearsall was shot and injured during an alleged attempted robbery in Union Square in August 2024. He made a full recovery. NBC News contributed to this report.

headlines.title: San Jose high school athletic trainer accused of sexual battery
headlines.description: A high school athletic trainer was accused of sexual battery and owning child sexual abuse material (CSAM), San Jose police said on Wednesday. Police said they responded to a report of sexual battery at Archbishop Mitty High School on Oct. 8 around 7:30 p.m. There, officers contacted a 16-year-old female student, who said a man was providing care for her sports-related injury when he sexually battered her and recorded it on his phone, authorities said. Officials said the suspect was identified as 31-year-old Kelvin Chiu, an athletic trainer for the school. Detectives obtained a search warrant for the suspect, his home and vehicles, according to the police department. Authorities said Chiu was located and apprehended in Fremont on Oct. 9. After serving a search warrant at his home, detectives found CSAM on Chiu’s phone, the police department said. The suspect was transported and booked into the Santa Clara County Mail Jail in connection to crimes related to annoying or molesting a minor, production and possession of CSAM and sexual battery, according to authorities. Cynthia Shaw, the director of communications for Diocese of San Jose, said Chiu has been an employee of Archbishop Mitty High School since May 2025. Shaw said Chiu was placed on administrative leave. Due to Chiu’s position of trust, the police department said there may be additional victims. They encourage anyone with information about these cases to contact Detective Camarillo and Detective Widmer of the San Jose Police Internet Crimes Against Children (ICAC)/Child Exploitation Detail (CED) Task Force via email: 4576@sanjoseca.gov, and 4581@sanjoseca.gov or by calling 408-277-4102. Shaw’s statement reads, in part: “Our first concern is for the student and family, and for all of our students and families. We recognize the impact a situation of this nature may have on our students, and the school’s Counseling teams will be available to speak with students who may need additional support. “We encourage any victim-survivor to come forward and report incidents of improper conduct either historically or currently occurring at any diocesan parish, school or ministry. To report any other concerns, we encourage individuals to first contact their local civil authorities (law enforcement). Once a report is filed with the local civil authorities, individuals are encouraged to contact the diocesan Office for the Protection of Children & Vulnerable Adults at (408) 983-0113. All reports are confidential to protect the rights of the victim. Reports to the Diocese are accepted by either online submission or by phone. For online submission, please use the following URL to access our secure third-party reporting server designated for this purpose: https://opcva.ethicspoint.com or contact our toll-free 24-hour reporting hotline at 844-372-1691.”

headlines.title: Chevron refinery in Richmond issues alert on flaring activity
headlines.description: Chevron issued an alert for people who live near its refinery in Richmond due to flaring activity at the facility. Chevron says the public does not need to evacuate or take any action. It says flares are highly regulated safety devices used to relieve pressure during the refining process. Officials say it also helps keep their equipment operating safely. Chevron says a team is working quickly to stop the flaring.

headlines.title: California sues to block planned closure of National Archives at San Francisco
headlines.description: California Attorney General Rob Bonta is taking the Trump administration to court in hopes of blocking the planned closure of the San Francisco National Archives facility in San Bruno. Bonta said the closure would scatter more than 175 years of historical records across the country, creating new challenges for the families, researchers and tribal communities that rely on them. “We are here to protect generations of California history,” Bonta said Wednesday. “Records that belong to the people of this state need to remain here to be accessible to the people of this state.” The federal government has said the San Francisco National Archives collection would be spread out among five National Archives facilities across the country and the San Bruno facility would be closed to cut costs. Bonta argues the government failed to properly consider the impact or give the public a meaningful opportunity to weigh in. “[The National Archives and Records Administration] did none of that,” Bonta said. “Instead, it decided unilaterally and behind closed doors to pack up our history and ship it away.” The Trump administration did not immediately comment on the lawsuit. NBC Bay Area’s Ali Reid has more in the video report above. San Bruno Aug 24 San Bruno Aug 20 New effort underway to save National Archives sites, including one in San Bruno

headlines.title: Defunct tiny home builder's customers say prosecutors are ‘angry for us'
headlines.description: With a less-than-two minute hearing on Wednesday, several Bay Area homeowners who say they collectively lost hundreds of thousands dollars to a failed tiny home builder, got a flash of justice. “Well, I’m happy that justice is moving forward,” said Martinez homeowner Lara Zanzucchi. “I came here today because I wanted justice for this case.” The brief hearing was for Colton and Austin Paulhus, the co-founders of Anchored Tiny Homes. They face a 35-count “felony complaint” that claims they billed customers like Lara for more than $1,000,000 “despite performing no work and supplying no materials.” The complaint says the pair conspired and diverted more than $600,000 from their company “for expenses and activity unrelated to company projects.” Lawyers told the judge they’re exchanging evidence, but neither Paulhus brother entered a plea. All the court and customers heard from the builders was a video acknowledgment that they’ll appear at a future hearing. “Yes, your honor,” they said in unison. This hearing is a mere blink of an eye in this two-year-long scandal. But former Anchored Tiny Homes customers told NBC Bay Area that they welcome any progress probing the builder’s sudden collapse and where their money went. “I feel very confident that justice is on the way,” said former customer Janet Kaufman. Prosecutors and Colton Paulhus’ attorney declined to comment. But, outside the courthouse, Austin Paulhus’ lawyer, Blair Goss briefly took questions. NBC Bay Area asked if Austin Paulhus if cooperating. “Absolutely,” Goss said. “We’re here in court. We’re happy to cooperate, and see where things went wrong and make sure everything gets right.” NBC Bay Area then asked if Austin Paulhus would testify against his brother, Colton. “I have no comment at this time,” Goss said. After the hearing, several customers told me they met privately, for the first time, with the prosecutors handling this case. “I think just meeting the D-A and the lead investigator, I can tell where their heart is,” Zanzucchi said. Kaufman echoed that sentiment. “They’re there to do a job,” she said. ”And you could almost feel the energy that they’re angry for us.” Several former Anchored Tiny Homes customers said they will return to the courtroom whenever the Paulus brothers’ case is on the docket. The judge ordered the brothers back in court January 12th.

headlines.title: DOJ threatens legal action against California over alleged noncitizen voters
headlines.description: The Justice Department is threatening legal action against California unless state and local officials review a list of potential noncitizens on their voter rolls. Acting Deputy Attorney General R. Trent McCotter on Tuesday sent letters to California Secretary of State Shirley Weber and Los Angeles County Registrar-Recorder Dean Logan with a list of names of possible noncitizens identified by the federal government. The letters demand they review the list by noon on Thursday. “Allowing noncitizens to vote cancels citizen votes,” McCotter wrote in the letters, which were obtained by NBC News. McCotter wrote that the DOJ provided a password-protected thumb drive with a list of individuals the federal government “believes are likely noncitizens who were sent a vote-by-mail ballot” for the 2026 election. He asked that county election officials “segregate — not cancel — those individuals’ vote-by-mail ballots” until their citizenship status was determined. “This should not be controversial, as the criminal statute is clear: only American citizens may vote in federal elections,” a Justice Department spokesperson said in a statement. “It is a federal crime for noncitizens to vote in U.S. elections, and the DOJ is asking California to ensure that is not occurring.” Reuters first reported on the letters. Justin Levitt, an NBC News contributor who was a Justice Department official during the Obama administration, said the federal government has no authority supporting its demands. “They can send the letter,” he said. “California doesn’t have to do anything about it.” Federal law prohibits systemic list maintenance within 90 days of a federal election. At this point, less than three weeks out from Election Day, the only changes to the voter rolls can come from individualized information, like notification from the Social Security Administration that someone has died. A DOJ spokesperson said the department is asking California to sequester ballots, not change their voter list. In a statement Wednesday, Logan said his office had not accessed the thumb drive the DOJ provided “because doing so would conflict with established data privacy and information security protocols.” He added, “We do not consider the device a secure medium.” “Maintaining accurate voter registration records is a fundamental responsibility of our office,” Logan said in the statement. “Federal and state laws are clear on how voter eligibility is established — and any action to remove a voter from eligibility must be based on verifiable information, not assertions of unconfirmed data matching.” Weber said in a statement Wednesday that the DOJ did not provide a list of purported noncitizens to her office and that the administration lacked the legal authority for its request. “The USDOJ’s relentless efforts to unlawfully gain access to states’ protected voter data and purge voter rolls serve only to cause chaos and fuel public distrust in our elections,” Weber said in the statement. “California has robust state law requirements that only U.S. citizens can register to vote and that any non-eligible registrants are removed from the State’s voter rolls. My office and California election officials remain committed — as always — to ensuring a fair and smooth 2026 General Election.” Trump Administration 23 hours ago Immigration Oct 13 All registered voters in California receive mail-in ballots, which started going out on Oct. 5. The legal threats came amid a broader campaign by the Trump administration to zero in on what voting experts say is a relatively rare phenomenon of voting by noncitizen individuals. Trump has long made unfounded claims that voting is marred by widespread fraud. Election officials in several states — including Georgia, Connecticut, Nevada and Washington state — say they have received federal subpoenas in recent months for election records. Some officials said they fear these actions were designed to set up possible legal challenges after the midterm elections. “What we have seen is some groundwork laid out for postelection challenges,” said Stuart Holmes, the director of elections in Washington state. “Whether that’s the seizure of voting equipment, ballots themselves, tabulation equipment … we’re preparing for any and all eventualities in that case.” Nevada Secretary of State Cisco Aguilar, a Democrat, said officials in his state are also preparing for potential challenges to this November’s results. He added that he viewed the administration’s moves as “an effort to dissuade people from participating in the elections.” “You have a president who’s trying to choose the voter base rather than the voters choosing the elected, and that’s not how our democracy works,” he said in an interview. “It’s the people control our elections, and when you try to take that control out, you do it through intimidation, you do it through threats, and you do it by trying to dissuade people from participating.” Levitt agreed with the election officials’ conclusions. “Are they laying the groundwork to say that voting was fraudulent? Of course they are, 100% they are,” he said, referring to the Trump administration. “Is the boy who cried wolf going to cry wolf? Yes, that’s what the boy who cried wolf does.” Since Trump took office, his administration has brought over 100 cases involving allegations of voting by noncitizens. More than 154 million people voted in the 2024 election, according to the U.S. Census Bureau. During the second Trump administration, the DOJ has sought voter registration data from every state in the country. It has filed lawsuits against 30 states and Washington, D.C., for refusing.
headlines.source: Ryan J. Reilly and Jane C. Timm | NBC News

headlines.title: Shutoffs affect thousands of Bay Area PG&E customers
headlines.description: More than 11,000 PG&E customers in the Bay Area could see dayslong power outages starting Wednesday as part of the utility’s proactive shutoffs to avoid its equipment from sparking wildfires. PG&E implements what it calls Public Safety Power Shutoffs when there is a forecast of dry and windy weather that poses a high wildfire risk, and is shutting off power to about 88,000 customers across 29 counties for a period that could last from Wednesday evening through Saturday afternoon. In the Bay Area, that includes 4,705 customers in Alameda County, 1,605 in Contra Costa County, 3,027 in Napa County, 30 in Solano County, and 2,041 in Sonoma County. PG&E’s outage map website shows areas affected will include the Berkeley and Oakland hills, the Tri-Valley part of the East Bay, locations near Mount Diablo, and higher elevation areas north of Santa Rosa and Napa. PG&E spokesperson Tamar Sarkissian said customers started receiving notifications on Monday about the potential shutoff. People can visit pge.com/pspsupdates to find out if their location may be affected by the power shutoffs. The utility is planning to open more than 40 community resource centers in affected areas that will offer restrooms, device charging, Wi-Fi, bottled water and snacks, and other supplies. A list of the centers by county can be found at https://pgealerts.alerts.pge.com/ways-we-can-help/#crc-table. PG&E is also encouraging customers who may need additional support to contact 211, including those who rely on power for medical needs or who have a disability. National Weather Service forecasters say higher elevations in the North Bay will have particularly dry and windy weather starting Thursday that poses elevated risks of wildfires. High temperatures are expected to peak in the Bay Area on Friday, with highs in the 80s and 90s, before cooling off this weekend and early next week.

headlines.title: San Jose prepares for potential El Niño storms, flooding
headlines.description: San Jose is laying out its preparations for what could be a historic El Niño storm season as the city works to avoid the kind of extreme flooding seen in 2017. In 2017, extensive flooding along Coyote Creek forced thousands to evacuate and caused more than $70 million in damage. Now, nearly 10 years later, with predictions calling for potentially record-breaking El Niño storms, Mayor Matt Mahan said the city is proactively preparing to prevent flooding. “Right now, our teams are monitoring more than 60 locations with a history of flooding or landslides, and just last week, our Transportation Department held an annual storm coordination meeting to review emergency response procedures and make sure crews are ready,” Mahan said. The city will also use its new $90 million emergency operations center. The 11,000-square-foot command center will allow city and Valley Water leaders to coordinate a response. More than 80 emergency response leaders can come together there in less than an hour to make critical decisions about how to respond to an El Niño storm. “When a major storm or emergency hits San Jose, this is the place that we come to generate ideas, generate our directions or action plan and direct the support and response of all departments,” said Ray Riordan, director of the San Jose Office of Emergency Management. San Jose also has invested in swift-water rescue gear and equipment to help clear storm drains. The city is working to identify potential hotspots and sending crews to preemptively clean drains, check storm pumps and repair infrastructure. Officials know staff can’t be everywhere, which is why residents are urged to prepare. “Start with your home, clean your gutters and drains, inspect your roofs, seal gaps where water can possibly come in and most importantly, ensure trees have been trimmed and properly maintained,” said Lee Steckmest, an Office of Emergency Management CERT volunteer. “A little preparation can make a big difference.” Emergency responders said it’s also important to pack a go bag with essentials, including medications, important documents and a flashlight and establish an emergency evacuation plan with your family. Residents are also preparing for El Niño. Tree trimming and roofing companies are getting an unprecedented number of calls. “I mean, we’re getting a ton of calls, a lot of people are hearing the news, and they want to see if their roof is okay,” Daniel Thomas with Los Gatos Roofing said. From roofing services to tree trimming, companies are receiving more calls than usual. And those calls are coming in earlier than usual. “Usually, we’re getting calls as the storms are arising, trees are already looking like they’re going to fall over or they’re in the midst of falling, this year, its rare we’ve gotten so much time to prepare,” Robert Apolinar with San Jose Tree Service said. Los Gatos Roofing says the last few months have been slow, but now that’s quickly changing as the rainy season draws closer and the warnings about an El Niño winter grow louder. “A lot more calls, a lot more people just wanting us to come out there and jump up on the roof and give them extra assurance,” Thomas said.

headlines.title: Caltrans works to raise flood-prone Highway 37 ahead of El Niño storms
headlines.description: As California prepares for a potentially powerful El Niño, Caltrans is racing to raise a flood-prone North Bay highway before the winter storms arrive. Highway 37 near Mare Island has flooded repeatedly over the years. On Wednesday, crews were working to raise parts of the highway near the island by about three feet. Additional work will require a 55-hour closure of the highway in both directions between Mare Island and Sears Point staring next Friday night. The highway is scheduled to reopen by 5 a.m. on Monday, Oct. 26. “We’re going to be grading the top level of asphalt down that’s started to crack so we get to the sub-surface,” Bart Ney with Caltrans said. “Then we’re going to be adding concrete, a fill in to get it up, and then paving back over the top of it.” Caltrans said the work is designed to help reduce flooding risks on the vital commuter route.

headlines.title: San Francisco nonprofit marks 75 years helping residents with developmental disabilities
headlines.description: A San Francisco nonprofit will be celebrating its efforts to move residents with developmental disability forward. The Arc San Francisco is marking its 75th year. To celebrate, it will hold its 24th Annual WorkLife Awards on Thursday to recognize workers, employers and community partners who have helped ensure opportunities for Bay Area residents who are often overlooked or underestimated. “We work with adults with intellectual and developmental disabilities, and support them, partner them, so they can achieve whatever they want in their lives,” Senior Director of Workforce Inclusion at The Arc San Francisco Virginia Wan Nogueira said. That could include living independently, getting a job, taking classes, or support managing healthcare. The nonprofit has a robust workforce development team with a host of tasks, including resume writing and job interview prep. “When they get the job, we support them with onboarding and maintaining their job through job coaches who work very closely with our employers to ensure that when they are working here, that things are going well, that our participants and our employers get the support that they need,” Nogueira said. “I talk to leaders in hospitality and other partners that we have and let them know that we have other options and other platforms where we can hire many different skills and Arc is one of them,” Director of Human Resources Beacon Grand Dale Dadoy said. “When an I/DD worker comes into work, they bring in their own whole self. They do not take the position for granted, they do their best and if they can’t do their best, they communicate they raise their hand and that is when leaders like me come in and say what do you need because everyone deserves that kind of success in the workplace.” “If we can give a helping hand to those who are I/DD, such as me, then we can help other people get jobs in this society, in the hotel, or even anywhere,” banquet houseman Tuan Le said.

headlines.title: Naked woman statue in San Francisco taken down
headlines.description: A landmark statue of a naked woman along San Francisco’s Embarcadero is coming down. The 45-foot illuminated statue was positioned in front of the Ferry Building for the past 18 months, but crews started taking it down Tuesday. The statue was originally created for the 2015 Burning Man festival and was later moved to the city as part of an outdoor art initiative called the Big Art Loop. It originally was supposed to only stay for six months. The piece was created by Bay Area artist Marco Cochrane and now is available for sale or lease on his website.

headlines.title: Netflix to cut about 6% of worldwide staff
headlines.description: Netflix is eliminating about 6% of its employee roster, or roughly 1,000 jobs, in a round of layoffs announced internally Wednesday, according to a source with knowledge of the matter. “Our mission — to entertain the world — is ambitious, and delivering on it requires us to be disciplined about where we prioritize our people and resources,” Netflix co-chief executives Greg Peters and Ted Sarandos said in an email to staff members Wednesday. The news was first reported by The Wall Street Journal. The source with knowledge of the matter confirmed the newspaper’s reporting was accurate. Netflix remains one of the titans of streaming, but it has struggled to boost user engagement on the platform. The service’s users watched more than 97 billion hours of content in the first half of 2026, an increase of 2% year-over-year, according to the company’s most recent quarterly earnings report. “Overall, we’re not growing as fast as I want us to, and we’re working on making that move faster,” Sarandos said at Bloomberg’s annual media conference late last month. Netflix is expected to report its third-quarter financial results next Tuesday. The majority of the job cuts will be concentrated in Netflix’s product, technology, legal and human-resources teams. Peters and Sarandos said the streaming firm will “continue to invest aggressively in high impact areas” while also “making focused choices across the business so we can keep delivering for our members, partners, employees and investors.” In recent months, Netflix has looked for ways to boost subscriber engagement, including adding live sports programming and video podcasts licensed from third-party companies such as Bill Simmons’ The Ringer. Netflix’s layoffs come as other major Hollywood studios look to reduce costs and streamline operations. The Walt Disney Co. has cut hundreds of jobs this year under new Chief Executive Josh D’Amaro, according to a source familiar with the matter. David Ellison’s Skydance is widely expected to shrink its work force across Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery.
